proof_summary: If primes \(p,q\) have different final digits, \(pq\le150\), and neither divides \(d\), invertibility modulo \(pq\) makes one of the first 150 terms divisible by both, a contradiction. Applying this to selected small-prime pairs successively forces \(2,5,3,7\mid d\), hence \(210\mid d\); the bound then excludes both \(11\mid d\) and \(13\mid d\), while \(11\cdot13=143\le150\) gives the final contradiction.
